$comment: Browser tool surfaces the task harness can drive. `aux` uses the runtime's own agent loop (runs.start). Every `mcp` adapter is driven by the SAME generic tool-calling loop and the SAME model (tests/benchmarks/tasks/run.mjs), so differences between rows come from the browser and its tool surface, not from the agent. `command` is spawned as an MCP stdio server; `env` is merged over process.env; `requires` lists binaries that must be on PATH or the adapter reports not-installed.

aux-loop.note: Aux's S5 durable tool-call loop (agent-loop engine) — the A/B-gate counterpart to aux (planner). Same model, same corpus; the gate compares pass@1, model calls and spend before planner.ts can be deleted.

aux-mcp.note: Aux's MCP server over the loopback API; the harness starts a runtime, mints a workspace-scoped connection and saves one task per benchmark task with its start page attached.

aux-code.note: QuickJS code mode through the same scoped runtime and model loop; compare against aux planner on fixture tasks without changing the model.

playwright-mcp.note: Microsoft Playwright MCP (aria snapshot + refs) on headless Chromium.

agent-browser.note: Vercel agent-browser MCP mode, if the binary exposes one in your version; otherwise adjust the command.

browser-use-mcp.note: browser-use's MCP server; the installed browser-use harness CLI itself is a scripting tool, not a task agent.
